citations.quote:
The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $S=\overline{\mathbb D}\setminus\{p_1,\ldots,p_a\}$, where $a\ge1$ and the $p_i$ are distinct points of $\partial\mathbb D$, with the standard disk complex structure and mutually disjoint holomorphic strip-end coordinates $(s,t)\in[0,\infty)\times[0,1]$ and a compact complement. The source is oriented by its complex structure. Let $E\to S$ be a smooth complex rank-$m$ bundle, $m\ge1$, with a smooth oriented totally real rank-$m$ boundary subbundle $F$. Let $D$ be an actual smooth real-linear Cauchy–Riemann operator, with symbol $2\overline\partial$. In each end suppose a specified smooth complex frame gives the exact boundary planes
$$F(s,0)=\mathbb R^m,\qquad F(s,1)=\prod_{j=1}^m e^{i\theta_{ij}}\mathbb R,\qquad 0<\theta_{ij}<\pi,$$
and identifies the actual coefficient equation with
$$D_i=\partial_s+i\partial_t+B_i(s,t),\qquad \sup_{t\in[0,1]}|B_i(s,t)|\longrightarrow0.$$
Here $B_i$ is smooth and real linear. Assume fixed smooth metrics which in these frames and coordinates are the product metrics outside a compact set. Target components transform with the Cauchy–Riemann symbol under a change of source coordinate; globally the target is the bundle of $E$-valued $(0,1)$-forms, with the harmless factor two included in its local coefficient convention.

Put $\gamma=\min_{i,j}\{\theta_{ij},\pi-\theta_{ij}\}>0$ and choose $0\le\delta<\gamma$. Let $\rho$ be a smooth positive function equal to $e^{\delta s}$ on every sufficiently far end. Let $X$ be the $H^1$ completion of smooth compactly supported boundary-compatible sections, with norms given by a fixed finite compact atlas and the specified end coordinates; put $Y=L^2$. Define $X_\delta=\{u:\rho u\in X\}$ and $Y_\delta=\{f:\rho f\in Y\}$. Then
$$D:X_\delta\longrightarrow Y_\delta$$
is bounded Fredholm over $\mathbb R$. There is a bounded two-sided parametrix whose two errors are operator-norm limits of finite-rank maps. In particular the kernel is finite dimensional, the range is closed of finite codimension, and the inverse from the Hilbert kernel complement onto that range is bounded.

This is a theorem about the specified actual operator and its exact completed boundary domain. It does not identify its index, prove that a geometric polygon satisfies the end hypotheses, establish surjectivity or universal regularity, or assert nonlinear compactness or gluing.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $E\to\overline{\mathbb D}$ be a smooth complex vector bundle of rank $m\ge1$, with complex multiplication $J$, and let $F\subset E|_{\partial\mathbb D}$ be a smooth oriented totally real real subbundle of rank $m$. Let $P$ be a smooth real-linear first-order operator on sections with exact Cauchy–Riemann symbol: for real smooth $h$ and smooth $\xi$,
$$P(h\xi)=hP\xi+h_x\xi+h_yJ\xi.$$
Use smooth positive definite metrics and finite smooth charts to define $H^r(E)$ by weak derivatives for integers $r\ge1$. Let $X_0$ be the $H^1$ closure of smooth sections with boundary values in $F$, and put $X_q=H^{q+1}(E)\cap X_0$, $Y_q=H^q(E)$ for integers $q\ge0$. Only the zeroth boundary condition is imposed.

There is a smooth global complex frame of $E$ and an integer $k$ in which the boundary condition is
$$F(e^{it})=e^{ikt}\mathbb R\oplus\mathbb R^{m-1}$$
and the actual operator is $\partial_x+i\partial_y+B$ with smooth real-linear zeroth-order coefficient $B$. Equivalently, before this reduction, if $C(t)$ is the complex matrix whose columns are any smooth periodic oriented real frame of $F$ in any global complex frame, then
$$k=\frac1{2\pi i}\int_0^{2\pi}\frac{(\det C)'(t)}{\det C(t)}\,dt.$$
Such frames exist, and this integer is independent of both choices.

Every actual realization $P_q:X_q\to Y_q$ is bounded Fredholm with real index $m+2k$. Its kernel is the same set as the $H^1$ kernel, its range is $Y_q\cap\operatorname{Ran}P_0$, and inclusion in $L^2$ identifies its real cokernel with that of $P_0$. For $\xi\in X_0$ and $P\xi=f\in H^q$,
$$\|\xi\|_{H^{q+1}}\le C_q(\|f\|_{H^q}+\|\xi\|_{H^1}).$$
The inverse of $P_0$ from its $H^1$ kernel complement to its closed range is bounded, and its restriction gives a bounded range inverse $H^q\cap\operatorname{Ran}P_0\to X_q$. The statement applies to an actual geometric linearization along a smooth disk with oriented totally real boundary. It does not assert its surjectivity, compute a Heegaard domain formula, or supply a puncture or gluing theorem.

Assume Countable Choice. Fix $m\ge1$ and angles $0<\theta_j<\pi$ for $1\le j\le m$. On the strip $S=\mathbb R\times[0,1]$ impose the real product-plane boundary conditions $u(s,0)\in\mathbb R^m$ and $u(s,1)\in\prod_j e^{i\theta_j}\mathbb R$. Let $H^1_\theta$ be the completion of smooth maps satisfying these conditions and compactly supported in the $s$ direction, for the norm
$$\|u\|_{H^1}^2=\|u\|_2^2+\|u_s\|_2^2+\|u_t\|_2^2.$$
The real linear operator $D=\partial_s+i\partial_t$ extends to an isomorphism $H^1_\theta\to L^2(S;\mathbb C^m)$. Put $\gamma=\min_j\{\theta_j,\pi-\theta_j\}>0$. Its inverse satisfies
$$\|D^{-1}f\|_2\le\gamma^{-1}\|f\|_2,\qquad \|D^{-1}f\|_{H^1}\le\sqrt{\gamma^{-2}+5}\,\|f\|_2.$$
For $0\le\delta<\gamma$, set $w(s)=e^{\delta|s|}$, $H^1_{\theta,\delta}=\{u:wu\in H^1_\theta\}$ with norm $\|wu\|_{H^1}$, and $L^2_\delta=\{f:wf\in L^2\}$ with norm $\|wf\|_2$. Then $D:H^1_{\theta,\delta}\to L^2_\delta$ is an isomorphism and
$$\|D^{-1}f\|_{H^1_{\theta,\delta}}\le\frac{\sqrt{\gamma^{-2}+5}}{1-\delta/\gamma}\,\|f\|_{L^2_\delta},\qquad \|wD^{-1}f\|_2\le\frac{\|wf\|_2}{\gamma-\delta}.$$
These are estimates for the constant linear asymptotic model. They make no assertion about nonlinear strip decay, a variable-coefficient operator, or its Maslov index.

Assume Countable Choice and put $S=\mathbb R\times(0,1)$. For $k=1,2,3$ there is a bounded linear extension $H^k(S)\to H^k(\mathbb R^2)$, using no boundary condition. The spaces have the estimates $H^1(S)\subset L^4(S)$, $H^2(S)\subset C^0(\overline S)\cap L^\infty(S)$, and $H^3(S)\subset C^1(\overline S)$, with bounded supremum norms in the last two assertions. In particular
$$\|fg\|_{H^2}\le C\|f\|_{H^2}\|g\|_{H^2}.$$

Fix smooth $\rho\ge0$ equal to $|s|$ outside a compact interval, with bounded derivatives, and $\delta\ge0$. Set $w=e^{\delta\rho}$ and $\|u\|_{H^k_\delta}=\|wu\|_{H^k}$. The same embeddings hold with $w|u|$, or $w(|u|+|du|)$ for $k=3$, bounded by the weighted norm. Products satisfy
$$\|fg\|_{H^2_\delta}\le C_\delta\|f\|_{H^2_\delta}\|g\|_{H^2_\delta},\qquad \|du\|_{H^2_\delta}\le C_\delta\|u\|_{H^3_\delta}.$$

Let $h(s,t,z)$ be smooth up to the boundary for $z$ in a finite-dimensional ball about zero, with bounded mixed derivatives of source order at most two and every finite target order on smaller target balls, and $h(s,t,0)=0$. Then $u\mapsto h(s,t,u)$ is a smooth map from the open subset of $H^2_\delta$ whose supremum lies in that ball to $H^2_\delta$. Its derivatives are the ordinary pointwise derivatives of $h$. On a sufficiently small bounded norm ball the remainder $Q(u)=h(s,t,u)-h_z(s,t,0)u$ satisfies
$$\|Q(u)-Q(v)\|_{H^2_\delta}\le C\bigl(\|u\|_{H^2_\delta}+\|v\|_{H^2_\delta}\bigr)\|u-v\|_{H^2_\delta}.$$
All statements hold componentwise for finite-dimensional real or complex targets.

Step 1.1 includes delta0 and keeps the zero-force inverse; higher kernels equal the original kernel.
Step 2.1 treats each end independently, including the one-end case.
Statement retains strictly transverse angles and weight strictly below the gap; coefficient derivatives through2 are bounded, no threshold or zero-mode end is added.
Step 1.1 obtains tangential derivatives in the exact H1 domain and recovers normal derivatives from the equation, never imposing higher normal traces.
Steps 1.1–4.1 inherit only the actual countable-choice analytic suppliers; no arbitrary inverse or uncountable family of selections is used.
